A computer implemented method of access control for a restricted resource of a resource provider in a network connected computer system, wherein a blockchain data structure accessible via the network stores digitally signed records validated by network connected miner software components, the method including: identifying an access control role definition for access to the resource, the role including a specification of access permissions; defining a cryptocurrency for indicating authorization to access the resource, the cryptocurrency being formed of tradable units of value associated with records in the blockchain and wherein transfer of the cryptocurrency between records in the blockchain is validated by the miners; receiving a request from an authenticated resource consumer for authorization to access the resource; and submitting a blockchain transaction to the miner components to transfer a quantity of cryptocurrency to a consumer record in the blockchain, the transaction including an identification of the role, such that the consumer record identifies that the consumer is authorized to access the resource in accordance with the role definition.

outputs.L3:
The method provides a way to control access to a restricted resource in a networked computer system by using records maintained on a blockchain. Instead of relying solely on a conventional centralized access-control list, the system uses blockchain-based transactions and records to indicate whether a particular user, device, service, or other resource consumer is authorized to access the restricted resource.

As part of the method, a role definition is identified for the restricted resource. The role definition specifies the access permissions associated with a particular role. For example, the role definition may indicate whether a resource consumer is permitted to read data, modify data, execute a service, administer settings, or perform other operations involving the restricted resource. The role therefore serves as a defined set of permissions that can be assigned or granted to an authorized consumer.

The method also defines a cryptocurrency that represents authorization to access the restricted resource. The cryptocurrency may be implemented as tradable blockchain-based units, such as tokens or coins, that can be recorded, transferred, and verified through blockchain transactions. Possession or allocation of the cryptocurrency, in association with a particular role, serves as evidence that the corresponding resource consumer has been granted access rights under the applicable role definition.

An authenticated resource consumer may submit a request for authorization to access the restricted resource. The resource consumer may be a user account, computing device, application, service, or other entity capable of interacting with the networked computer system. Before authorization is granted, the consumer is authenticated so that the system can associate the request with a verified identity or record.

In response to the request, a blockchain transaction is generated or processed to transfer an amount of the cryptocurrency to a blockchain record associated with the authenticated resource consumer. The transaction also identifies the relevant role definition. Once recorded on the blockchain, the transaction provides a verifiable indication that the consumer has been authorized to access the restricted resource according to the permissions specified by the identified role. The system can then evaluate the blockchain record to determine whether the consumer holds the required authorization and, if so, permit access to the restricted resource in accordance with the corresponding role definition.
outputs.L4:
A computer-implemented access control method is provided for controlling access to a restricted network resource by using a blockchain-based authorization mechanism. In the method, one or more authorization roles are defined for the restricted resource, such as an administrator role, a read-only user role, a service-consumer role, or another permission-bearing role. Each role is associated with one or more cryptocurrency units, tokens, or blockchain-recorded assets that represent the right to access the restricted resource under the permissions assigned to that role.

When a consumer, user, device, or service seeks authorization to access the restricted network resource, an authorization entity initiates a transfer of one or more role-linked cryptocurrency units to a blockchain address, wallet, or account associated with that consumer. The transfer is submitted to a blockchain network and is validated by miners or other blockchain consensus participants. Once the transfer is confirmed and recorded in the blockchain ledger, the consumer’s blockchain record contains evidence that the consumer has been assigned the corresponding authorization role.

An access control system associated with the restricted resource verifies authorization by inspecting the blockchain. For example, when the consumer requests access to the resource, the access control system may identify the consumer’s blockchain address and determine whether the address holds the required role-linked cryptocurrency unit or has received a validated transfer corresponding to the required role. If the blockchain record confirms that the consumer possesses the appropriate role-linked unit, the system grants access to the resource in accordance with the permissions associated with that role. If the required blockchain record is absent, invalid, revoked, expired, or otherwise insufficient, access is denied or limited.

Because the role assignment is represented by a miner-validated cryptocurrency transfer, the authorization record is tamper-resistant, auditable, and independently verifiable. The blockchain provides a distributed record of when the role-linked unit was transferred, which entity transferred it, and which consumer received it. This allows the system to maintain authorization state without relying solely on a centralized permission database. Changes to access rights may be performed by transferring additional role-linked units, returning or burning previously assigned units, transferring revocation tokens, or otherwise updating the blockchain state to reflect a modified authorization status.

In this manner, the method uses blockchain transactions as access-control credentials. The confirmed ownership or receipt of a cryptocurrency unit associated with a defined role serves as proof that the consumer is authorized to access the restricted network resource according to the permissions assigned to that role.
outputs.L5:
A computer-implemented solution refers to a process, method, or system that is carried out using computer technology. Instead of being performed manually, the task is executed through software, hardware, or a combination of both. This approach is widely used in modern industries because it can improve speed, accuracy, scalability, and efficiency.

For example, a computer-implemented method may involve collecting data, processing it through an algorithm, storing the results in a database, and presenting the output to a user through an interface. Such methods are common in fields like finance, healthcare, manufacturing, education, and communication. Online banking systems, medical diagnostic tools, automated inventory platforms, and learning management systems are all examples of computer-implemented technologies.

One major advantage of a computer-implemented system is automation. Repetitive tasks can be performed with minimal human involvement, reducing the risk of error and saving time. Additionally, computers can analyze large amounts of information much faster than humans, making them useful for decision-making, prediction, and optimization.

Security and reliability are also important considerations. A well-designed computer-implemented system should protect sensitive data, prevent unauthorized access, and continue functioning correctly even when handling high volumes of activity. Developers often use encryption, authentication, backups, and monitoring tools to support these goals.

In conclusion, a computer-implemented approach plays an essential role in today’s digital world. By using computers to perform tasks, organizations and individuals can achieve better performance, greater consistency, and more effective management of information.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent-style paragraph for an invention using blockchain transactions and tradable digital currency units to assign role-based access control permissions to resource consumers.
counterfactuals.output: In some embodiments, a computer-implemented access control system is provided in which role-based access control permissions for one or more protected resources are represented, assigned, modified, or revoked through blockchain-recorded transactions involving tradable digital currency units. A resource consumer may obtain, receive, or be delegated one or more digital currency units, tokens, or tokenized permission instruments associated with a defined access role, wherein ownership, custody, staking, transfer, or redemption of the digital currency units is recorded on a distributed ledger and is used by an access control engine to determine whether the resource consumer is authorized to perform one or more operations on a protected resource. A smart contract may define mappings between token attributes and access roles, including permission scope, duration, hierarchy, delegation rights, usage limits, revocation conditions, and compliance constraints, and may automatically update role assignments in response to blockchain events such as transfers, expirations, burns, locks, or escrow releases. Upon receiving an access request, the access control engine may verify the resource consumer’s cryptographic identity, query the blockchain or an indexed ledger state to confirm possession or control of the corresponding digital currency units, resolve the applicable role-based permissions, and permit or deny access to the requested resource based at least in part on the verified ledger state. In this manner, access permissions may be made portable, auditable, transferable, monetizable, and programmatically enforceable while maintaining a tamper-resistant record of authorization changes.
